title: A burn or scald — cool it with running water
applies_to: Skin burned by heat: hot water, steam, cooking oil, a flame, or a hot surface.
also_called: should i put ice on it

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: First Aid
International Society for Burn Injuries, Practice Guidelines for Burn Care

steps.text: Look at where the burn is and how big it is. Their own flat hand is a rough guide to size.
Get them away from the heat. Turn it off at the switch or the tap if you can do it safely.
Hold the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes. Start as soon as you can, and still do it even if some time has already passed.
While it cools, take off rings, bangles, watches, and tight clothing near the burn. The skin will swell.
After cooling, lay clean cling film loosely over the burn in one layer, or use a clean dry cloth.
Keep the rest of the body warm. Cooling a large burn can chill the whole person.
Get them to a doctor if the burn is bigger than their palm, is on the face, hands, feet, or over a joint, or if the skin looks white, brown, or leathery.
Call an ambulance for a burn that goes all the way round an arm or a leg, or if they breathed in smoke or steam.

do_not: Do not put ice, iced water, butter, oil, toothpaste, ash, or any cream on a burn.
Do not pull off clothing that is stuck to the burn. Cool it with the cloth still in place.
Do not wrap cling film round and round a limb. Lay it on in one loose layer instead.
Do not use cotton wool or anything fluffy. The fibres stick to the burn.
escalate_if: They are coughing, hoarse, or have soot around the nose or mouth — the airway may be burned. Call now.
The burn came from electricity — the injury goes deeper than it looks. Get them seen even if the skin looks fine.
They start shivering, look pale, or get sleepy — say this on the phone.
It is a baby, a small child, or an older adult — get them seen even for a small burn.
The burn came from a chemical — keep rinsing with running water and tell the crew what it was.
